# Editing & pacing

Family: **Visual craft** · 22 ideas · [index](../index.md)


## Edit

### Something new on screen every 1.2–2.5 s
<a id="edit-change-every-1-5-2-5s"></a>

Change something (cut, layout swap, label, card, animation) every 1.5–2.5 s (L01, L02). Rahul measured at roughly every 1.2–2 s in every reel; his sponsored Flipkart reel was the fastest at 1.2 s.

**How:** CapCut/VN: split on every new phrase and alternate face, graphic and label; check gaps on the timeline. ffmpeg: scdet / select='gt(scene,0.3)' to count cuts.

> A visual change (cut, layout swap or animation) every 1.5–2.5 s

### Graphic yap: one overlay every ~2 s
<a id="edit-graphic-yap-overlay-2s"></a>

Chaotic graphic yap: overlay camera-roll images or clips about one every 2 s, so a 60 s video needs about 30 images. A full-screen version cuts 9:16 Canva images over the talking.

**How:** Edits/CapCut: Overlay → add image, trim each to ~2 s; Canva for full-screen 9:16 cards.

> About one new visual every 2 s. For a 60 s video, collect about 30 images

`edit` · formats: reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches: all · stated · from [L06](../sources/L06.md)

### Train a cut rhythm, then break it
<a id="edit-trained-rhythm-break"></a>

A regular cut cadence (Caleb's example: 12 frames / 36 frames) trains the viewer; breaking the pattern then emphasises the big moment.

### Axial jump cuts every 3–6 words
<a id="edit-axial-jump-cuts"></a>

Talking head: cut from the medium shot to a digital punch-in on the same angle every 3–6 words to hit emphasis words.

**How:** CapCut/VN: split on the emphasis word and scale the next segment to 115–130%; shoot 4K so the punch-in stays sharp.

> Axial jump cuts (medium shot to digital punch-in on the same angle) every 3–6 words

`edit` · formats: yt-long, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches: all · observed · from [L07](../sources/L07.md)

### Cut every breath and pause
<a id="edit-cut-breaths-no-dead-air"></a>

Jump cuts remove breaths (the ReCut method in action). Rahul's reels have no dead air: under 2.5% of 100 ms windows sit 25 dB below the median level.

**How:** ReCut app (~$20) or the editor's silence removal; ffmpeg silenceremove, or cut on faster-whisper word timestamps.

> Breaths and pauses are cut out; there is no dead air.

### Speed ramps: dead time, beats, top rep
<a id="edit-speed-ramps"></a>

Subtle ramps on browser scrolls and screen recordings remove dead time (L07); the L08 teaser syncs ramps to percussive hits; our gym default ramps into the top rep.

**How:** CapCut: Speed → Curve (custom); VN: speed curve; shoot 60 fps for smooth slow sections.

### Cut on the beat or on motion
<a id="edit-cut-on-beat-motion"></a>

Our edit blueprint sets cut rules (on the beat or on motion) and travel uses a wide → close-up rhythm. Khandala cut every 1.5 s, which lands on 80 and 120 BPM beats (2 or 3 beats per shot), so music could be added later.

**How:** CapCut: Beat → auto-mark beats, snap cuts; ffmpeg: trim each shot to 45 frames at 30 fps.

> Cuts every 1.5 s, so it sits on the beat of any 80/120 BPM track.

`edit` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches: all, travel, gym · our-take · from [SP](../sources/SP.md), [KH](../sources/KH.md)

### Face check before using any frame
<a id="edit-face-check"></a>

Never use frames where the mouth is open or mid-word, the tongue shows, eyes are mid-blink or the angle is awkward; prefer a clear smile, a confident neutral or a candid look-away. The Khandala profile shot was replaced after this feedback.

> Never use frames where the mouth is open or mid-word, the tongue shows, the eyes are mid-blink or half-closed, or the face is caught at an awkward angle.

### Teaching format: template card, then a real example
<a id="l11-template-then-example"></a>

Each item = a template card (~2–3 s: numbered badge, the template typing on with blanks in yellow) followed by a real viral reel that used it (~2–3.5 s, full-frame with its own audio and a view-count pill). 7 pairs in 49.6 s; 48% of the runtime is other creators' clips.

**How:** For a 'N hooks / N edits / N settings' reel: say the pattern, then show one proof clip, ideally your own (reduces the C31 originality risk). Cut on the last word of the template; keep the same seated shot for every card so the examples feel like inserts.

> This is exactly what you want to see when you're X.

`edit` · formats: reel30, reel60, yt-short · niches: all · observed · from [L11](../sources/L11.md) · ⚠ [C31](../clashes.md#c31)

## Graphics

### Real screenshot beats an AI mock-up
<a id="l10-real-screenshot-not-mockup"></a>

For UI graphics such as an editor timeline, a real screenshot looks better than a generated mock-up. He shows both, back to back.

**How:** Capture the real screen (timeline, app, settings) and put it in a rounded dark card; keep generated mock-ups for things that don't exist.

> You could create a mock-up of your editor timeline, but a real screenshot would look much better.
